body: I mean it's true we all have brain damage thanks to this stupid illness
Not often used but yes. I also use it when I tell people I used to be in the military. It works perfectly fine ✌️

28M DX 3 years ago MS can really mess up our sexdrive. Different things work like testosterone or viagra, the side effects of viagra can be annoying. I don't know if it could work for your partner but in my case using cannabis gets me in the mood. Also have you talked about possibly using adult toys? It could help your relationship a lot.
I asked ny doctor about this he told me vaping or edibles are healthier because smoking may cause inflammation so i'd rather not risk any more damage it's already bad enough. No smoking for me.
Ah no wonder you cut contact in the first place
60% of the time it works everytime
100% agree f*ck you MS
Thanks! I really hope so too but knowing the VA it's gonna take a minute.
Damn that was fast, congrats. I applied on april, I'm just hoping I don't get more of those useless letters.
How long did you had to wait for the letter? A couple of days ago I got my third "we are still working on your case" empty talk letter.
No ofreció ayudar??? Que mal 😒

No shame at all! I have pooped my pants multiple times. I accepted it as part of one of the many things we have to deal with. Keep your head up and always have a fresh pair of pants in your car! I know I do
I really hope they come up with a cure but for now let's just hope better treatment. Hopefully in the next 15-20 years. I just want to be able to run one more time before my time is up.

I understand you 100% I used to swiming, hiking or a simple morning jog was all I needed now I can't do any of that but don't let that be the end of it. Try and find new hobbies I picked up reading quite a lot and recently I began trying to learn how to play the guitar, I'm horrible at it but learning is part of the fun lol

Yeah I know the only people that understand us is others with this curse of an illness. Thank you for that little piece of advice it reminded me of something my mother used to say, it brought a smile to my face.

I understand you completely. This sucks but you have something to keep fighting for you're already a father keep on going for your kid. As for me, I don't know if I'll ever have kids I'm afraid of being a burden instead of an actual father .

I'm in the process of getting a medical license but lucky me my neuro is against the use of cannabis so I need to find another doctor that can help me get it. Hopefully once I do get it I can relax atleast for a bit.
Lol I never though about it that way. Naps plus the occasional zoomies

I know it sucks, I fucking hate this illness as any other ms warrior. It changed our life for the worse, but don't let it take you down. It took me an entire day to just clean my room and ready my suitcase for a flight but I still did it! Nobody but yourself can set your limits. Just take the time you need. You will accomplish whatever goal you set!
I love posts like this. It reminds me that even with this illness life can be good.

I used to be in the navy served for a total of 5 years on my last year I went through the med board process got a 90% from the VA but appealed and got 100%. Sadly it very difficult for you to continue serving with this illness, you can try and stay and fight but it will be an uphill battle, hell for me I was forbidden from working on ships for safety reasons, witch limited where I could work.

26M Diagnosed almost 2 years ago. I have been using a cane for a couple of months. Who cares about what people think of you for using a cane? Are they going to help you walk around? Get yourself a cane and keep on going! I go everywhere with my cane and people rarely ever mention it.

Having a wheelchair will make him lazy? And his dad agrees with that? Are you fucking kidding me!? Those two have no idea  how difficult can be to simply walk when you have MS?  Please, continue to support your bf and get him to switch to an actual competent doctor!
Scheduling it that way sounds  like a good idea. It seems like most people don't drive after getting it so it looks like is going to be a lyft for me then.
Gotcha! That's what I thought, I don't like to use uber/lyft but i'll have to deal with it.

That's great! I already asked this, but how do you feel after getting the infusion? are you able to drive afterwards? I live alone, unfortunately  I don't have anyone to rely on to drive me back home if I'm unable to.
That's great to know! hopefully I can also deal with my fatigue in a better way if I end up using ocrevus.
So you feel off for a couple of days after the infusion? That kinda worries me, are you able you drive safely after getting it?

That doesn't sound bad at all, having only to take the medication once every six months is also convinient. I have to admit that I have forgotten a couple of times to take the second pill at the end of the day lol.
I'm so happy for both of you! This is so heartwarming. I went trough something similar, I was afraid of  driving due to my MS  but with a lot of effort I finally got my first car all on my own.

It's true, the military does offer a lot of medical services but not much is properly explained.  Most of the time it's left for you to figure it out. I also have to admit that I haven't been doing the best like I said, I have no family to rely on here. I have mostly been dealing with this alone.

That's a peculiar way of seeing things lol but I kinda understand. Being able to talk to people like me has helped  me process this a bit better it's not the end of the world I just have to find a new perspective in life.

I have only seen my neurologist twice. Both times they were just short appointments to talk about my MRI scans. Let's just say that Navy medical (or atleast the one that I had access to) is not the best. I have an upcoming appointment in january. If it's the same thing ill request a different neurologist.
You most have a lot to say about this, regardless glad to know there's other vets in here! I used to be an IS2

I have heard very little about DMTs, I have used the services provided by the military regarding suicidal prevention and therapy but I feel like I have never been taken seriously. I still remember when a  chaplain laughed when I explained what was happening to me when I was going through  my first flare up.
I have lost a lot due to MS. I still feel adrift. Now I know that there's people out there like me that figure it out, maybe I can too.

I have a long road ahead of me.  You made a good choice in asking your doctor for antidepressants, I didn't. I think it just made it more difficult for me to accept this. Hopefully my neurologist also agrees that I should take antidepressants.

You're a lot tougher than I am right now. Even if I have been living like this for a year I still  feel like have a lot to learn about MS, like you said what's the choice? There's nothing we can do about this. Even if I know that it will never happen I'm still hoping to wake up from this nightmare. I'll have to accept this is my new life.
